description:
## Goal

Give hidden macro roots the same persistent `RootBackendProduct` ownership as user roots, route macro execution directly through that product, then delete the BackendProgram scheduler bridge.

## Combined-head truth

`BuildMacroExecutable` still synthesizes backend production, waits on `FactKey::BackendProgram`, and reads a World projection. fz-tfn.9 made the handles canonical and shared, but it did not make the bridge authoritative. Keeping both retained products and the fact/map would require a second movement protocol.

## Strategy and proof

1. Persist macro-root product sessions with the same exact movement and retirement rules as user roots.
2. Make macro executable production read `RootBackendProduct(root)` content/generation directly.
3. Prove unchanged macro calls reuse the settled program; reached macro-source changes invalidate exact readers; unrelated and program-equal movement does no backend work.
4. Delete `Job::BuildBackendProduct`, `FactKey::BackendProgram`, `BackendProgramMap`, backend/native revision remnants, product-to-fact copying, synthetic completion identity, and bridge-only tests/docs.
5. Reassess root-level nested `Rc` after the map disappears. This ticket owns collapsing any handle whose second lifetime no longer exists; retained nesting requires a pointer-ownership proof.

## Acceptance

Macro and user roots consume one persistent product model. No backend fact/map mirror, revision bridge, deep clone, or compatibility path remains. Macro recursion, exact causality, canonical artifacts/runtime output, full macro/library/serial-matrix tests, formatting, check, strict clippy, and docs pass.
title: Delete the BackendProgram scheduler bridge after macro roots join persistent products
